item.title: Global Governance Forum concludes in Xiong'an New Area; delegates explore how China's tech advances can contribute to global governance
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-25 21:12:00
An attendee tests a robot during the 2026 Global Governance Forum (Xiong'an) in Xiong'an New Area, North China's Hebei Province, on October 23, 2026. Photo: VCG The 2026 Global Governance Forum (Xiong'an), held from October 23 to 25, concluded on Sunday in Xiong'an New Area, North China's Hebei Province, with artificial intelligence (AI) emerging as a major topic of discussion among international participants, who explored how China's approach to AI development and governance could offer lessons for the wider world. Under the theme "Rebuilding Confidence and Cooperation: Reforming and Improving Global Governance in a Transforming World," the forum brought together nearly 400 representatives from political, academic, strategic, business and youth sectors from more than 90 countries and international and regional organizations. Wang Yi, a member of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China Central Committee and Chinese Foreign Minister, attended the opening ceremony and delivered a keynote speech. Hosted by the Chinese People's Institute of Foreign Affairs (CPIFA), the forum provided a platform for participants to exchange ideas on reforming and improving global governance, with AI governance attracting particular attention. Among the recurring keywords in the discussions were practical applications, safety, risks and equitable access. The Global Times observed particularly strong attendance and lively exchanges at AI-themed sessions, where participants raised questions ranging from how AI could be applied to public services and traditional industries to how countries could manage emerging security threats and prevent a widening digital divide. Pan Jingyu, director of the China-SCO Countries AI Application Cooperation Center, told the Global Times that global AI governance is entering a critical period for jointly shaping rules, developing standards and building technological capacity. China has reached a leading position in AI development, Pan said, noting that the emergence of highly competitive Chinese AI models has attracted widespread international attention. Their affordability, innovative open-source ecosystems and technological capabilities have challenged the dominance of a handful of global technology giants, offering Global South countries new possibilities for leapfrogging in digital development, Pan said. Andrea Renda, director of research at the Centre for European Policy Studies (CEPS), believes China's approach to AI development could also offer useful lessons for Europe. "China is a pioneer in artificial intelligence," Renda said, pointing to its focus on applying AI in specific industrial settings and public services, with an emphasis on people-centered applications that improve everyday life. He noted that this approach could be particularly relevant to the EU, where high energy costs and established industrial structures make it important to use AI to strengthen existing industries rather than simply replace them. Speaking to the Global Times about his first visit to Xiong'an, Renda said he had studied the city's development model since the project was launched. He suggested that Xiong'an's experience could offer a blueprint for more sustainable global AI governance, with AI treated as a means to improve people's lives rather than an end in itself. However, he stressed that such a model should ensure local control over data and allow communities to benefit from the value created through technological development. Describing Europe as the "old continent," Renda noted that European cities cannot simply be rebuilt from scratch as Xiong'an has been. Nevertheless, he said the new area offers valuable lessons in energy management, AI, data governance, urban green spaces and the government's role in fostering innovation, which could help European cities find new ways to develop. A foreign guest shakes hands with a robot at the Global Governance Forum in Xiong'an New Area, North China's Hebei Province, on October 24, 2026. Photo: Hu Yuwei/Global Times While many participants saw opportunities in AI-driven development, others at the forum warned that unequal access to technology and growing security risks could undermine its benefits. Lyu Deqiang, president of the Singapore chapter of the Global Responsible AI Council, said the widening AI divide between countries makes fairness in global governance an increasingly urgent issue. He told the media that global AI governance is currently shaped largely by major powers and economies, including China, the US and the EU. Dialogues such as the forum were particularly meaningful because they gave smaller and medium-sized countries, along with other stakeholders, opportunities to voice their concerns and share perspectives. Pan also warned that AI security threats are evolving in two directions as the technology advances rapidly. On one hand, the weaponization of large language models and the use of AI in cyberattacks and defense are lowering the barriers to launching attacks. On the other, AI-specific threats, including prompt injection, model poisoning and unauthorized actions by AI agents, are becoming increasingly prominent. These challenges, he said, highlight the need for stronger international coordination on AI governance. Beyond discussions at the forum, Xiong'an itself offered international participants a firsthand look at how digital technologies can be integrated into urban governance. Some foreign guests visited Xiong'an's digital infrastructure facilities, learning about the city's cloud computing infrastructure and its concept of "three cities in one" — above ground, underground and in the cloud. The city's use of cloud-based data systems in public services also drew interest. During the forum, participants discussed how community-level data could help improve neighborhood management and provide more targeted services for elderly residents and people with disabilities. Some foreign visitors told the Global Times that it was their first time encountering the concept of three interconnected cities, describing it as a striking example of how innovative urban planning and digital infrastructure could be integrated into a city established only nine years ago. Jorge Agudero, a writer and scholar from Spain, told the Global Times that China's achievement in building Xiong'an into a technologically advanced, green and innovative "city of the future" in just over nine years was difficult for many foreigners to imagine.

item.title: 81st anniversary of Taiwan's recovery commemorated; DPP authorities' attempts to promote 'de-Sinicization' doomed to fail: expert
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-25 19:59:00
Photo: Screenshot from the WeChat account of the PLA Eastern Theater Command As multiple commemorative activities were held Sunday on both sides of the Taiwan Straits to mark the 81st anniversary of China's recovery of Taiwan, the Chinese People's Liberation Army (PLA) Eastern Theater Command released its first poster marking Taiwan Recovery Day, sending a clear message that the PLA would not tolerate or show leniency toward any attempts to separate the island of Taiwan from China and would deliver forceful blows against such actions, Chinese experts said. In an article, the PLA Eastern Theater Command recalled that on October 25, 1945, Taiwan returned to the embrace of the motherland. Taiwan's recovery was an important outcome of the Chinese People's War of Resistance Against Japanese Aggression, irrefutable evidence of the Chinese government's resumption of the exercise of sovereignty over Taiwan, and a crucial link in the historical facts and legal chain establishing Taiwan as part of China. The Taiwan Affairs Office of the State Council released a video reviewing how Chinese people fought together in a bloody struggle to achieve victory in the War of Resistance Against Japanese Aggression and Taiwan's recovery. The video also showcased the driving force behind advancing the process of national reunification and realizing the great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. On the island of Taiwan, commemorative activities were held in various places. A civic group organized a cultural relics exhibition in commemoration in Taipei, aiming to revive public awareness of history, UDN reported. At an event held at Taichung Park in Taichung, organizers displayed historical materials and photographs documenting Taiwan's resistance against Japanese aggression and its recovery and return to China. The event also featured young people from Taiwan reading quotations and articles left by people who resisted Japanese colonial rule during the 50 years from 1895 to 1945. Young participants from Taiwan chanted, "Return us to our motherland and restore the homeland of our ancestors!" The event was solemn and dignified, China Review News Agency reported. Zheng Jian, a professor at the Taiwan Research Institute of Xiamen University, told the Global Times that the solemn national commemorations and grassroots commemorative events on the island stand in stark contrast to the Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) authorities' longstanding efforts to downplay, dilute and distort the history of Taiwan's recovery. In education and public discourse on the island, the DPP authorities have avoided or removed historical facts related to Taiwan's recovery, favored ambiguous wording such as "the end of the war," and deliberately avoided acknowledging the core conclusions of victory in the War of Resistance Against Japanese Aggression and Taiwan's return to the motherland. Through curriculum changes and public opinion guidance, they have promoted "de-Sinicization," whitewashed Japanese colonial rule and fabricated a "Taiwan independence" version of history, deliberately severing the historical ties between Taiwan and the Chinese mainland and instilling a false understanding of history in younger generations, Zheng said. Such historical nihilism is essentially an attempt to undermine the one-China fact from historical and legal perspectives, he said. At a symposium marking the 81st anniversary of Taiwan's recovery held in Fuzhou, East China's Fujian Province, former Kuomintang chairperson Hung Hsiu-chu said Taiwan's liberation from Japanese colonial rule was not a gift that fell from the sky, but a restoration of national dignity won through the sacrifice of countless compatriots on both sides of the Taiwan Straits, who laid down their lives in the struggle. If "de-Sinicization" is allowed to continue poisoning the next generation, how can we face the martyrs who gave their lives for the cause? she asked. Meanwhile, Lai Ching-te and the DPP authorities not only distort historical facts by "only using the term 'the end of the war' while refusing to acknowledge Taiwan's recovery," but also collude with external forces to spread the false claim that "Taiwan's status remains undetermined," in an attempt to pursue "Taiwan independence" by relying on external forces and through military means, Zhang Junshe, a Chinese military affairs expert, told the Global Times on Sunday. In its poster titled "Remember Taiwan's Recovery, Defend National Unity," the PLA Eastern Theater Command used black-and-white documentary photographs to highlight the historical and geographical ties between the Chinese mainland and the island of Taiwan, as well as the shared sense of pride and national memory among people on both sides of the Straits. A map of Taiwan forms the visual centerpiece of the poster, alongside prominent banners bearing phrases such as "Taiwan's Recovery" and "venue of the surrender ceremony of Taiwan Province of the China war theater of the Allied powers." The poster demonstrates not only China's determination to safeguard the historical facts of Taiwan's recovery and the fruits of victory in the war against Japanese aggression achieved by people on both sides of the Taiwan Straits, but also its resolve to uphold the mission of safeguarding national reunification. Any attempts to dilute historical memory and promote "de-Sinicization" are doomed to fail, Zhang said.

item.title: Chinese research team achieves breakthrough in flexible solar devices
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-25 19:37:00
Photo: Screenshot from Xinhua A Chinese research team has developed a new strategy to overcome a longstanding challenge in flexible perovskite solar cells, enabling the production of large-area, commercial size flexible photovoltaic devices with power conversion efficiencies consistently exceeding 20 percent, the Xinhua News Agency has reported. Conventional solar panels are typically heavy and rigid. Flexible perovskite solar films, a promising focus of next-generation photovoltaic research, are lightweight and can conform to curved surfaces. However, scaling them up has long posed a major challenge, as both their power conversion efficiency and lifespan tend to decline significantly as their size increases, hindering their transition from the laboratory to real-world applications. The research team, which is led by professor Li Yaowen at Soochow University in East China's Jiangsu Province, has developed a novel research and development strategy called "decoupled co-deposition." The new study was published online in the journal Science on Friday. Li said that co-deposition is a crucial step in producing flexible perovskite photovoltaic films. During the process, perovskite crystallizes out of a precursor solution and attaches to a plastic substrate, forming a continuous film. However, as the film's area increases, the interfacial layer between the film and the plastic substrate tends to become uneven in thickness, as per Xinhua. The team investigated how the interfacial layer forms at the molecular level and identified a competitive mechanism, said co-corresponding author of the paper, professor Xu Guiying. When exposed to interfacial molecules and organic solvents in the precursor solution, hydroxyl groups on the plastic substrate face a molecular "either-or" choice. Some bind to the organic solvents, leaving the interfacial molecules unable to anchor themselves to the substrate. To address this problem, the team proposed "decoupled co-deposition," introducing a decoupling agent to break the bonds between the hydroxyl groups and organic solvents, allowing the hydroxyl groups to instead bind with the interfacial molecules. This helps the interfacial layer adhere firmly to the substrate. Over the past year, the team has worked with a company to scale up production beyond small-scale laboratory prototypes, producing a batch of large-area flexible photovoltaic devices with an effective area of 750 square centimeters. Their power conversion efficiency has more than doubled compared with previous levels, consistently exceeding 20 percent, Li said. "We will continue to strengthen the integration of industry, academia and research, using real-world industrial needs to guide our innovation and steadily advance the commercialization of flexible photovoltaics," Li said. China's installed photovoltaic power capacity reached 1.286 billion kilowatts at the end of July and has surpassed coal-fired power capacity for the first time, making PV the country's largest power source by installed capacity, according to the National Energy Administration on September 1. With the world's largest and fastest-growing renewable energy system, China supplies over 80 percent of photovoltaic modules and 70 percent of wind power equipment around the world, assisting the green transition in many countries and regions.

item.title: China-Europe Arctic shipping route draws strong demand from exporters amid global trade uncertainties
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-25 19:23:00
The first cargo ship of the China-Europe Arctic Express berths at Ningbo Zhoushan Port in East China's Zhejiang Province on December 6, 2025. Photo: VCG Chinese exporters and logistics companies are embracing the China-Europe Arctic shipping route, which offers shorter transit time and an alternative to traditional shipping corridors often exposed to geopolitical risks, industry analysts told the Global Times. With this year's Arctic shipping season drawing to a close, industry players are looking to expand services and extend operating time, highlighting the route's long-term potential to diversify global shipping networks despite seasonal and capacity constraints. New New Shipping Line Co, one of the operators of the Arctic route, told the Global Times that the Northeast Passage offers significantly shorter shipping distances than traditional routes between Asia and Europe. For example, a voyage from Shanghai to St. Petersburg typically takes 38 to 45 days via the Suez Canal, while the Arctic route can reduce the journey to 23 to 25 days, according to the company. The shipping company said that it has maintained regular seasonal operations along the Arctic route since 2023, deploying vessels for multiple round trips during the summer navigation windows from 2023 to 2025. Shorter voyages make the route competitive in terms of operating costs, while its distance from some traditional shipping corridors affected by geopolitical conflicts helps reduce risks, the company said. Sea Legend Shipping, a Shanghai-based shipping company, operated eight voyages in August and September during its first attempt at regular weekly services through the Arctic route, according to Chinese media reports. Preliminary figures showed that the service carried more than 14,000 20-foot equivalent units of export cargo, with nearly 80 percent originating from the Yangtze River Delta region. Shipments included new-energy equipment and cross-border e-commerce goods. The reports also noted strong demand from exporters in Yiwu, East China's Zhejiang Province, with some logistics companies reporting difficulties securing cargo space as businesses rushed to prepare shipments for the European Christmas shopping season. Cargo space on the China-Europe Arctic Express has been in particularly high demand this year, Zhong Zhechao, founder of One Shipping, an international logistics consultancy, told the Global Times on Sunday. The industry insider attributed the strong demand primarily to shorter transit time. Against the backdrop of a gradual recovery in Red Sea shipping and continued geopolitical uncertainties in the Middle East, the Arctic route offers an alternative to traditional shipping corridors through the Strait of Malacca and the Red Sea, providing more options for Asia-Europe trade, Zhong said. The route holds particular appeal for certain high-value goods, including new-energy batteries, solar and energy storage equipment, and electronic products. "Some of these products are sensitive to high temperatures, and the relatively cooler conditions along the Arctic route offer advantages for their transportation," according to Zhong. Compared with China-Europe freight trains, a flagship project and a landmark brand of the Belt and Road Initiative (BRI), the Arctic shipping route offers comparable transit time. The two can complement each other, Zhong noted. Despite growing interest of Chinese exporters, seasonal restrictions remain a major obstacle to the route's expansion. New New Shipping Line said that the conventional navigation window runs from mid-July to mid-to-late October. As Arctic Sea ice increases after October, navigation conditions deteriorate, and shipping operations would not resume until ice conditions improve the following summer. The company said that it is advancing the construction of vessels with higher ice-class ratings to improve navigation capabilities in icy waters, gradually extend the operating season and move toward more regular services. It noted that demand for Arctic cargo transportation continues to grow across a diverse range of products, and that it will further optimize vessel deployment according to market needs. Despite the challenges, interest in Arctic shipping is extending beyond China, with countries such as South Korea actively exploring related services, according to Zhong. In the longer term, the Arctic route holds considerable potential for diversifying international shipping corridors and strengthening supply chain security reaching out to BRI partner countries and beyond, analysts said. As navigation conditions evolve and icebreaker technology and related infrastructure advance, the navigable season could become longer, further enhancing the route's strategic importance in the global shipping network, said Zhong.

item.title: Xi exchanges congratulations with Belgium's King Philippe over 55th anniversary of ties
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-25 17:19:00
CHINA / DIPLOMACY Xi exchanges congratulations with Belgium's King Philippe over 55th anniversary of ties By Xinhua Published: Oct 25, 2026 05:19 PM Updated: Oct 25, 2026 06:39 PM
Chinese President Xi Jinping and Belgium's King Philippe on Sunday exchanged congratulations on the 55th anniversary of diplomatic relations between the two countries. Xi pointed out that over the past 55 years since the establishment of diplomatic relations, China and Belgium have upheld the principles of mutual respect, equality, mutual benefit and win-win cooperation, and bilateral relations have developed steadily. Exchanges and cooperation between the two countries across various fields have yielded numerous highlights and fruitful results, while people-to-people ties have grown increasingly close, he said. Xi said he attaches great importance to the development of China-Belgium relations and stands ready to work with King Philippe to take the 55th anniversary of bilateral diplomatic relations as an opportunity to guide China-Belgium all-round friendly cooperative partnership to new heights, and to make new contributions to promoting the sound and steady development of China-EU relations. In his message, Philippe said that since the establishment of diplomatic relations, Belgium and China have developed extensive and diversified cooperative relations. Recalling President Xi's successful state visit to Belgium in 2014, which left him with fond memories, Philippe said he firmly believes that the two sides would build on the achievements of the past 55 years to further promote open dialogue, expand practical cooperation and deepen mutual understanding. Belgium stands ready to develop balanced and mutually beneficial relations with China, address common global challenges, and promote peace, stability and sustainable development, he said.

item.title: China's national civil service exam registration closes, with over 6,000 applicants competing for a single position: media
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-25 10:07:00
Candidates exit the exam venue after the national civil service examination on November 30, 2025. Photo: CNS Photo Saturday marked the final day to apply for China's 2027 national civil service examination, with competition for the most sought-after positions exceeding 6,000 applicants per post, chinanews.com reported on Sunday. As of 5 pm on Saturday, more than 6,000 applicants had passed the initial review for a first-level police inspector position or below with the Yanbian border management detachment of the Jilin immigration inspection general station. The position had only one vacancy, putting the competition ratio at more than 6,000 to 1, according to the report. Yanbian, located in Northeast China's Jilin Province, is the only autonomous prefecture of China's Korean ethnic group, according to the Xinhua News Agency. In addition, several other positions have attracted thousands of applicants for a single vacancy. For example, a position at the Gongyi survey team under the Henan survey team of the National Bureau of Statistics had 5,534 applicants who passed the review for just one opening, with six applications still pending review. According to thepaper.cn, citing statistics from Huatu Education, as of 4 pm on Saturday, 3.025 million applicants had passed the qualification review, bringing the overall average competition ratio to 85 applicants per position. In addition, 83 positions had received no applications by the time registration closed. These "zero-application" positions are concentrated in several types of government agencies, particularly maritime safety administrations, railway police bureaus, and immigration inspection stations under border management authorities, according to thepaper.cn. Some positions at meteorological bureaus, National Bureau of Statistics survey teams, and customs authorities have also received no applications. Such positions typically have strict professional or academic requirements and involve demanding working conditions, such as working on the water, serving in grassroots roles in remote areas, or working shifts. Positions in remote and less accessible regions may also attract fewer applicants, as the pool of who meet the requirements is relatively small. Global Times

item.title: Teodoro charges at China with a paper shield
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-24 13:52:00
Philippines Secretary of National Defense Gilberto Teodoro Jr. delivers his speech during a plenary session of the International Institute for Strategic Studies (IISS) Shangri-la Dialogue Defense Summit in Singapore, 31 May 2026. Photo: VCG Philippine Defense Secretary Gilberto Teodoro Jr. has once again been huffing at China, claiming that if China were to remove the Philippine ship that is illegally "grounded" at China's Ren'ai Jiao, it would constitute a so-called "act of war." He also warned that if Chinese personnel boarded the vessel, it could trigger the US-Philippines Mutual Defense Treaty. Yet no sooner had he made these threats than he began backpedaling, clarifying that an “act of war” does not necessarily mean the two countries would enter a “state of war,” as “only the President and Congress can declare war.” Teodoro is charging at China with a shield made of paper, only to retreat behind Marcos and the US before China has even made a move. This performance essentially lays bare his opportunism and cowardice. Teodoro's remarks were based on an unverified Philippine media report claiming that “China was considering 10 countermeasures against the Philippines,” including removing the grounded ship, blocking supplies, sanctioning Philippine politicians, reducing oil and fertilizer supplies, and restricting tourism. Teodoro admitted that he had not even read the report, yet he was already rushing to issue warnings. This suggests that he knows perfectly well the price of provoking China and that the Philippines cannot afford to pay it. For all his tough talk, he is effectively crying out in pain in anticipation of the consequences. China has indisputable sovereignty over Ren'ai Jiao and its adjacent waters. The China Coast Guard carries out law enforcement operations to safeguard rights in waters under its jurisdiction in accordance with the law. Its demand that the Philippines remove the illegally grounded warship is legitimate and well-founded. If the Philippines continues to gamble on provocations, persists in illegal intrusions and the reinforcement of structures at Ren'ai Jiao, or even attempts to forcibly break through China's law-enforcement controls, China will certainly take all necessary measures to firmly safeguard its territorial sovereignty and maritime rights and interests. The Philippines should harbor no illusions on this matter. The further it goes in provoking China, the heavier the blows it will suffer. By then, it will be too late to try to salvage the situation by hiding behind others. Last month, Philippine media reported on a letter allegedly signed by Teodoro and addressed to a Central Intelligence Agency (CIA) official. According to the reported contents, Teodoro pledged that if he were to assume presidential power in the future, he would continue strengthening the US-Philippines alliance and pursuing a hard-line policy toward China. He also reportedly planned to manufacture maritime friction at Ren'ai Jiao during an ASEAN foreign ministers' meeting to portray China as a country "bullying a smaller nation." The Philippine Department of National Defense promptly denied the letter's authenticity, saying it “is false and fake,” but provided no evidence. The authenticity of the letter remains to be verified. Nevertheless, the pattern of behavior described in it closely mirrors Teodoro's own conduct, lending further weight to the suspicion that Teodoro is "on a mission." He is attempting to manufacture friction to serve his personal political ambitions, using his hardline stance toward China as a token of allegiance to external forces. Before trying to intimidate China with cries of an "act of war," Teodoro had better think carefully about the consequences of his words. No external power will foot the bill for his reckless rhetoric, and any so-called "treaty" will become nothing more than a scrap of paper in the face of risks of this magnitude.

item.title: Ninety years on, the great Long March spirit is a light shining on the world: Global Times editorial
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-23 00:36:00
Marching toward prosperity. Illustration: Liu Rui/GT The great Long March spirit has been deeply etched into the DNA of Chinese society. It is the determination to rise to challenges and to persist for the long haul; it is the courage to fear no sacrifice and to dare to try; it is the clarity to face reality and actively seek change; and above all, it is the original aspiration of standing with the people through life and death, sharing weal and woe, and striving arduously. The 90th anniversary of the victory of the Long March of the Chinese Workers' and Peasants' Red Army was commemorated at a grand gathering in Beijing on Thursday morning. General Secretary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee Xi Jinping, also Chinese president and chairman of the Central Military Commission, attended the gathering and delivered an important speech. Xi stressed that the great spirit of the Long March demonstrates the power of loyalty, truth, justice and unity. As an important part of the spiritual lineage of the CPC, it transcends time and space and remains evergreen. It will always be a precious treasure and a powerful driving force inspiring us to overcome difficulties and forge ahead courageously. The Long March was a beam of light that burst forth from the Chinese nation at its darkest hour. It showed the world clearly that, even in an old China mired in darkness with no visible way out, there was a group of people striving with all their might to build a new China. In the book The Life Millennium: The 100 Most Important Events and People of the Past 1000 Years, published by the American Time-Life Books, scholars from around the world jointly selected 100 events that shaped the world from 1000 to 2000 AD. The Long March of the Red Army was one of three historical events from China to make the list. It profoundly inspires people that as long as one remains firm in will and unyielding in the face of setbacks, a way out can always be found through continuous exploration, and an entirely new path can be opened. From Edgar Snow to Henry Kissinger, from Nelson Mandela to Fidel Castro, many observers and strategists have pondered why this Long March in the East was able to succeed. To this day, whenever China astonishes the world with technological breakthroughs or reshapes perceptions with development miracles, the world still asks: "How do the Chinese do it?" These questions all point to the same answer: We have found the right path - a path of never yielding, always moving forward, and never retreating. The Long March is both a spiritual treasure that inspires the Chinese people and a display of the Chinese nation's resilient character to the world. Today, the term "Long March" has become a shared name for any arduous journey that ultimately reaches its destination. In this sense, the value of the Long March lies not only in the arrival itself, but in the act of continuing to set forth, again and again. After the victory of the Long March, the nation did not stop: It kept marching through the flames of the War of Resistance Against Japanese Aggression, kept advancing on the tide of reform and opening-up, and continues to advance under the call of the new era, all the way toward the great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Today, the great Long March spirit has been deeply etched into the DNA of Chinese society. It is the determination to rise to challenges and to persist for the long haul; it is the courage to fear no sacrifice and to dare to try; it is the clarity to face reality and actively seek change; and above all, it is the original aspiration of standing with the people through life and death, sharing weal and woe, and striving arduously. Ninety years on, the great Long March spirit no longer belongs only to history; it is a light that grows ever brighter and shines upon the world. Currently, global governance is experiencing a "darkest hour": climate change, the North-South divide, geopolitical conflicts, and the undercurrents of deglobalization. Old paradigms are failing, and new rules have yet to take shape. Solving many major issues requires long-term planning and sustained effort that transcend political cycles and short-term gains and losses. The spirit of firm conviction, unity and cooperation, and unyielding struggle transcends national borders and ideologies. It inspires humanity to overcome adversity and pursue a brighter future. This both suggests that global governance needs to blaze new trails toward common development, common security, and common prosperity, and helps the world better understand the spiritual bedrock of the Chinese nation, enabling outsiders to better grasp where this "enabling great power" is heading. "Where the spirit lies, there lies the strength." The great Long March spirit resonates with the Chinese nation's cultural tradition of constant self-improvement and has gained new contemporary meaning in the process of Chinese modernization. While it is no longer possible for China today to replicate the march back then, this spirit will always remain, proving to the world that the Chinese nation possesses extraordinary resilience. After decades of struggle, China has long since become the world's second-largest economy and is comprehensively advancing the great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation through Chinese modernization. The enduring national resilience behind the great Long March spirit has been a key factor in creating this development miracle. It is the confidence that allows China to navigate storms and seize the historical initiative, and it also provides a stabilizing expectation for a world full of uncertainty. In the 1980s, Zbigniew Brzezinski, who once served as US national security advisor, walked with his family along the route once taken by the Red Army. He later reflected: "The Long March is more than an epic of almost unmatched heroism." Today, more and more foreigners are coming to China to retrace the Long March route, and places like Loushan Pass have once again become a popular destination for visitors. This is one indication that the great Long March spirit is increasingly needed by the world. As a spiritual monument that the Chinese nation has offered to the world, its importance will become even more prominent in the future. As military writer Wang Shuzeng once described: "The Long March belongs to that category of events in human history which, even after the passage of long years, continue to be sought after by people." "The history of the Long March has never faded; the road of the Long March continues to extend." For China, on the new journey, the Long March has no endpoint. To carry forward the great Long March spirit is to always maintain a high-spirited posture of storming passes and seizing fortresses, to continue the arduous trek on the journey of Chinese modernization, and to respond to all risks and challenges with an unstoppable fighting spirit. It is to both successfully navigate the Long March of our own generation and infuse a world marked by turbulence and transformation with confidence and strength from the East.

item.title: Ukraine's awkward position: Dependent on the US, powerless to push back

Ukraine Illustration: Liu Rui/GT Tension between the US and Ukraine has once again erupted into the open. Recent remarks by US Vice President JD Vance have laid bare a long-standing yet often obscured reality in US-Ukraine relations: Ukraine is not a formal US ally, and Washington does not want it to join NATO. Vance also called on Ukraine to stop striking Russian energy facilities. His comments appear to mark a clear boundary of US interests underpinning its Ukraine policy. The US may support Ukraine, but that does not mean it will underwrite every demand Kiev makes. Ukraine can rely on American aid, but it cannot expect Washington to stand unconditionally on its side. Vance has not articulated a brand-new policy. His statement is a public restatement of the current US administration's consistent position. The previous US administration, by contrast, stressed the moral imperative of supporting Ukraine, tying Ukrainian security closely to European security and US credibility, fostering a political relationship that resembled an alliance - despite the fact that Ukraine is not a NATO member, nor does it have a mutual defense treaty with the US. That it is not a formal ally has always been true. What stands out now is that the US no longer blurs this line deliberately, but proactively spells it out publicly. "Ukraine is trapped in an awkward, painful position. It cannot do without US assistance, yet it holds no leverage over Washington," Zhang Hong, a research fellow at the Institute of Russian, Eastern European and Central Asian Studies at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences, told the Global Times. Why is the US choosing this moment to publicly reaffirm this status? The answer lies in Vance's other demand: "Ukraine should stop attacking Russian energy facilities." An earlier diesel fuel deal struck between the US and Russia had already opened rifts in US-Ukraine relations. Compared with Ukraine's battlefield priorities, the US prioritizes its own energy market positioning and domestic political pressures. Compounding this, Washington has delayed deliveries of a batch of weapons to Ukraine. By partially cutting the aid pipeline while explicitly defining the bilateral relationship as non-allied, the US is essentially creating diplomatic cover to ratchet up pressure on Kiev. Should Ukraine's military actions run counter to core US interests, Washington can potentially scale back support and recalibrate its policy, laying full blame for escalation at Kiev's door. Aid is a discretionary favor, while rolling back support is seen as a legitimate policy choice - this has become the underlying logic of the US' Ukraine strategy. This does not mean Ukraine has lost its strategic value to the US. "In the European theater, the Ukraine crisis remains a key instrument for the US to sustain transatlantic security bonds. The US, in turn, retains sway over Europe's security agenda and reaps economic gains from defense industrial cooperation," Zhang explained. Toward Russia, the Ukraine crisis also serves as a vital topic for US diplomatic maneuvering. Whether negotiating ceasefire terms, security consultations or potential future energy and economic accords, Washington keeps the Ukraine crisis alive to preserve room for bargaining with Moscow, he added. Washington's support for Ukraine has never been an open-ended, unconditional moral obligation, but a strategic choice weighed rigorously against costs and benefits. Clearly, Ukraine's interests and grievances are never Washington's priority. Even when it comes to making the kind of deals Washington wants, Ukraine lacks the leverage to deliver. Ukraine's mineral resources available for potential deals are valued at around $500 billion, while potential joint projects between the US and Russia are worth as much as $14 trillion. By comparison, Ukraine's bargaining power is overwhelmingly outmatched. Ukraine has tried to tie itself to Europe, hoping European leaders would lobby Washington to sustain aid. Yet Europe maintains its own interest calculations, and the support it can offer Kiev is steadily dwindling. This leaves Ukraine stuck in a dilemma. The US is deliberately decoupling its own interests from Ukraine's aspirations. It has no objection to continuing to use the Ukraine issue to pressure Russia, yet refuses to assume treaty obligations for Ukraine's security goals. Partnership continues when Kiev's military moves align with Washington's objectives; when interests collide, Ukraine's demands are the ones usually sacrificed. From the moment Washington clarified the boundaries of US-Ukraine relations, one truth emerges: Ukraine has always been a geopolitical tool for the US, never its core interest. This unequal dynamic of dependence and limited bargaining power has left Ukraine in an awkward and passive position from the start.
